arutpa:T377:15: Bring camphor, solitary friend! This is the time my husband comes; let us celebrate the feast of eyes under the lotus feet of our lord. Know that this is not just staying under the five elemental states; it transcends the elemental states, goes beyond the sound-state, and shines above the supreme sound-state. If you celebrate the feast of eyes for that form, it will bring sweet grace to every world and every living being.
arutpa:T377:78: O foolish girl, listen as I tell you the reason why the time when the graceful one, my lord, the handsome dancer in the hall who is capable of all things, embraces us, will not come in the dark night: the light of the body of my unique master transcends the spoken earth up to the primal sound, goes even beyond the supreme sound-space, and shines inside and outside, filling all.
arutpa:T341:2: False qualities and maya vanished as true knowledge appeared; the golden-lighted ray arose and dawned upon the mountain of true qualities. All members of the path of truth surrounded to worship at the feet, standing and singing praises. O my supreme vast light that granted me every virtue, O my mother, please arise and grace us with your awakening.
arutpa:T272:9: O great life flourishing in the unobstructed Chidambaram, O sole God shining in the middle of the boundless, great ray, you have graciously listened to the persistent prayer I, your servant, have made. May this body of mine always become a destructionless golden form!
arutpa:T127:44: O gazelle-eyed maiden resembling a sword, possessing a ruby-like form, joined to the forehead-eyed lord of Tiruvarur! Are not those who saw the feet of thy devotees like those who conquered the worlds, attained true wisdom, and dwell in the sky like the moon surrounded by stars?
arutpa:T173:2: O mountain that grants the state of Shiva yoga, where one receives the ambrosial nourishment of the full rising moon!
arutpa:T277:6: O flame of true wisdom and bliss rising high in the sacred Chidambaram; O fire of growing rays, sun of growing fire, art growing in the midst of the sun; O king ruling beyond the great silent expansive space; O fruit of supreme bliss ripened for me to taste sweetly within my melting heart!
arutpa:T161:158: I have no season to perform austerities; I am a witless one who practices vanity in the false worldly path—do you have grace for me? O Shiva, the glowing light everywhere, beyond all comparison, O three-eyed god, I have not understood your intent.
arutpa:T272:8: O great life shining in the painting-like Chidambaram, O god shining in the middle of the revealing ray, you have graciously filled your ear with the prolonged prayer I, your servant, have made. May this attached body of mine always become a destructionless golden form!
arutpa:T316:469: The state of mantra, the state of moon, the state of chant, the state of secret.
arutpa:T342:3: Sleep vanished, the sun appeared, my longing ceased, sing this poem! I tasted the sweet ambrosia, sing this poem!
arutpa:T348:79: O sun of auspicious arising, of supreme peace, of great flourishing action, noble and great.
arutpa:T46:1: O god worshipped by devas in rich, cool Thanigai where the bright sun-ray hits the clouds and passes beyond—does grace exist for me, who fell, desiring even the stream of hot tears of the adorned lady who bedazzles anyone with her piercing gaze?
arutpa:T1:13: Can a vile worm seize a mighty fire? Can a deer leap across the sky? Can a mouse taunt a strong tiger? Can the wing of a fly painfully move a huge mountain? Can a mere speck of dust shatter a diamond? Can darkness come and surround the sun? Can rain mingle with the wind? No, it cannot. Just like that, can sorrow, delusion, anger, pettiness, or distortion ever touch those who wear the lotus feet of your golden feet, O Lord full of love, upon their heads? O Murugan, growing in the lofty shrine at Kandakottam in Chennai with your glorious fame! O divine jewel of your face, divine jewel of the front face, divine jewel of the six faces!
pavai:1: On this good day filled with the full moon of Margazhi, come for the water-bath! Come, maiden of fine ornaments! O prosperous, precious young girls of Aypadi! Narayanan—whose eyes are red like the sun and moon on a dark cloud-colored body, young lion of Yashoda with lovely-eyed gaze, son of Nanda with the sharp spear and cruel duty—will grant us the drum so that the whole world praises us. Immerse yourselves, O friends!
pavai:8: See, the lower sky has turned white, and the little buffaloes have spread out to graze! The other children who are going have gone; we have come to stop you and call you. O maiden filled with delight, arise! If we go and worship the god of gods who split the demon's mouth and struck down the wrestlers, crying out in compassion he will grant us grace, O friends!
pavai:13: Singing the glories of him who tore the bird's beak and plucked out the evil demon, all the children have entered the pavilion. See, the morning star has risen, Jupiter has set, and the birds are chirping! O maiden with lush, dark-red-lined eyes, will you lie in bed instead of plunging in and bathing to your heart's cool content? On this good day, abandon deceit and join us, O friends!
pavai:22: Like those who, losing all pride as kings of the vast earth, come and sit right under your royal couch, we have come and gathered here. Like the lotus flower with a chiming bell mouth, will your red eyes open just a little bit and look upon us? If you look upon us with your two eyes, like the moon and the sun rising, our curses will fall away, oh friend.
tolka:501: Giving a proper noun without its matching kin-word is colloquial usage, not the way of poetry.
arutpa:T157:39: Oh cool moon dwelling in Kotika, praising Namasivaya within the heart, running...
arutpa:T157:58: Like the moon in the sky, a gem-like water-lily blossom, a pure gold block thriving in the village...
arutpa:T157:199: Our gain at Kodungunram, praised by great ascetics and learned nine siddhas—the full-blazing sun...
arutpa:T158:129: Who is the god that spreads like the sky, cools like the moon, bears a majestic scepter, and is as sweet as honey—those who went to the sky...
arutpa:T158:473: As the bright sun passes the sky and our days pass away, alas, do we not tremble as the planets pass?
arutpa:T158:495: Shall I call it reality, or illusory creation, or lightning, or falsehood, or illusory dust—when called reality...
arutpa:T159:14: Is it today, tomorrow, day or night—in the days to come, I know not, wretched as I am! Drinking the cool nectar of your grace, oh mother like the assembly-thriving one, this dog-like one lives on through the days.
arutpa:T160:49: An ocean without shores or banks, overflowing and full as all the surging rivers of many religions enter and mingle; a state seen as eyes everywhere; a tree that spreads the shade of devotees and dispels all delusion; a floral pond; a moon coming as a wisdom-red water-lily blossom; God capable of all things, God of gods.
arutpa:T160:66: Like the bee that has drunk the honey of a fragrant flower, all who have tasted and rejoiced in the growing supreme bliss become united and fused, reaching a state beyond the phenomenal; what is that natural state? O Lord who stands alone while all worldly calculations and conventions cry out in defeat, hard for anyone to see here, supreme deity beyond all religious dogmas!
arutpa:T160:96: Like a mother who leaves an ignorant boy in a fierce forest at night during total, blinding darkness, not knowing his mind, and follows behind him—when the darkness of illusion grows, in the worldly wilderness of sense objects, alas, witless and fainting in bewilderment, you left me behind according to your just rule and vanished; oh, what is the wonder of your grace, O Supreme!
arutpa:T150:126: In the town where the Lord of Ottriyur desired Uma, there is a wonder: at night a triumphant lotus bloomed while in a pond below a water-lily closed, they say. Oh ladies with golden breasts, on what day is the moon waning near those who desired you? Tell me, companion, what is this?
arutpa:T112:9: Knowing a child's fault, a mother does not get angry; she bears it. Is there no justice for you to bear this dog's fault? With my heart tormented like the waning moon, crying aloud in distress, won't you call me to come?
arutpa:T122:10: What shall I say of the beauty of the holy one in the temple called gold? My heart has not understood it in the least. If the three lights called lightning grow dim, what shall I, your slave, say of his beauty? Will I see it one more time?
arutpa:T197:42: Oh my two eyes, what great penance has anyone in any world done? The two ancient ones searched without seeing and are still trying to see. You have seen and risen high, gazing at the supreme light that dispels the brightness of the twelve suns, in the temple where great kings worship and praise, oh noble ones.
arutpa:T138:4: Even if Brahma and Vishnu seek the Lord of sacred Ottriyur, borne by the bull, He is hard to meet at the junction. My precious lord has not drawn near yet. The evening hour has come, alas! The moon pours fire. Full of anxious thought, oh friend, I know not at all what to do.
arutpa:T141:7: The dark-throated one who wears the wild-jasmine, the thoughtful one, dear to my eyes as breath, dear as a mother, the handsome hero of Ottriyur does not embrace me to his flower-garlanded shoulder. At this evening hour the moon leaps up—what will it do to me, my friend? I can bear it no longer!
arutpa:T141:10: The sacred dancer who performs with the skull of the departed as his vessel, the donor of Ottriyur who makes seekers go mad—he has not joined me yet. If that cruel moon, seeking me, approaches, what will it do, my friend? I can bear it no longer!
arutpa:T7:26: Worn out in heart by the sorrow of a fleeting life like lightning, I stood longing to drink the nectar of your grace. If you push me away calling me a great sinner, what shall I do? Is it not just for a mother to bear the fault committed by her child, my lord? Can you not bear it? O gem of Thanigai, who is equal to yourself, living reality filling everything as a living witness!
arutpa:T19:3: Lest I fall into the superficial delusion of foolish women with lightning-like waists, let me mingle with supreme yogis who meditate on you, and place your sacred feet upon the head of this slave—oh blazing light residing on the shining hill of Thanigai, a great boon even for our lord who wears the braided locks!
arutpa:T46:2: Do you possess grace even for me, who am lower than a dog that gnaws the bare bone stripped of tough flesh, sinking deep in the cesspool of women with spear-like eyes? Oh god worshipped by deities in sacred Thanigai, rich with wonderful fertility where the sun's chariot driver whips his glowing horses so they scatter light everywhere among the fragrant bamboo gems!
arutpa:T163:12: The joy felt by those who sat in bliss—surrounded by spring twilight, cool groves, lotus ponds, a fitting moonstone terrace, a delightful sleeping cot upon it, white-wood and jasmine bowers, milk-like flowing moonlight, a solitary gentle breeze, a sweet-singing lute with vibrant strings, and affectionate playful words mingled with secret chastity—equals the shade of your dancing feet's lotus flowers, O Healer in Velur who makes devotees' disease of worldly birth vanish, Granter of wealth, Lord of the world, praised by the ocean-surrounded earth!
arutpa:T316:759: O moon that forever spreads cool rays like milk and shines brightly so the upper sky glows!
arutpa:T319:2: O great reality hard for anyone to comprehend, O mother, my father, my lord, my king! O deity who granted me a unique form unhindered by clouds, fire, wind, the expanse of the sky, the sun, the ocean, the ocean-girdled earth, elements, or birth! O nectar of Gnanasithipuram inhabited by those rich in virtue and noble qualities, my sleep has broken!
arutpa:T274:4: Cool moon, unique red flame, fire of truth and potential, shining light, light within light, lamp nestled within the true heart for all worlds to thrive, nectar of wisdom granted as desired, treasure of virtue, focused state, O substance enacting the cosmic dance in the public hall.
arutpa:T274:17: Supreme reality shining in consciousness, lord shining in supremacy, grace experiencing Shiva, cool moon that clears religious barriers, good opportunity of moon-full nectar, true righteous path, sole path's companion, lord, father, mother, rare great boon, hard-to-praise treasure, O substance enacting the cosmic dance in the public hall.
arutpa:T341:4: Even hard minds melted as the golden light was seen, the night cleared, many devotees arrived singing, dancing, praising, and blending with love; good people, true sages, yogis and others approached and surrounded you, O treasure of virtue, O supreme vast flame, my god, please arise and grace us.
arutpa:T341:5: The dark evening and whole night have cleared, the golden ray glowed upon the hill of wisdom, scholars have strung garlands of words and stand praising, all those of the pure Sanmarga assembly come and surround in continuous garlands, the celestials draw close and say 'be blessed', O supreme vast flame adorned with my garland, my lord, please arise and grace us.
arutpa:T342:1: Night has dawned, I attained the twin feet and rejoiced, thus let us hum; I consumed the milk-nectar, thus let us hum.
arutpa:T342:6: The waves have ceased, the red flame has appeared, the transcendent light has risen, thus let us hum; the worship has borne fruit, thus let us hum.
arutpa:T295:3: I do not sleep with my eyes; even if I sleep, I said there is is no dream other than uniting with my lord—was it because of this, or did I say I would enter the place where he dwells in the moonlit night that knows no counting? I know not whether it was because of this or that. The female companion spoke, calling me an untamable woman, and her face hardened. She who raised me with great grace also became a hostile stranger. Others remained uttering unending blame. I know not the divine will of the lord Nataraja.
arutpa:T257:8: Light growing richly with conscious powers manifesting in glowing fire, in salt, in matchless light, in flame, on the upper tile, in heat, in the inner dancing play, in the beginning and end, in clear color, in formlessness, in all operative actions; O hill of sweet Sivananda, sky beyond experiential joy, essence of wisdom, gem, pupil of my two eyes, my life, my wealth, storehouse of my life, companion that subdued the bounding monkey-mind within and gave me true bliss, treasure of pure Siva Sanmarga, O lord Nataraja of the supreme vast flame.
arutpa:T257:10: Light of grace holding the countless joyful masters and powers that grow in the sky, in the opportunity of the sky, in the formlessness of the sky, in the nature of the sky, at the base of the sky, in the middle and crown of the sky, in color, in arts, in the great expanse, in eternal strength, in complete boon, and in the rest; purest nectar which, even if combined and consumed with honey, milk, sugar, and clustered fruits, cannot be matched; form of bliss rising high in the color of cool moonlight, essence of bliss, treasure of pure Siva Sanmarga, O lord Nataraja of the supreme vast flame.
arutpa:T257:19: O lord Nataraja residing within the scientific consciousness standing in the true state of Sanmarga—truth which is the experiential Siva-turiya difficult to comprehend mingling with all arts, all-powerful god, boundless ocean of grace, fruit, sugarcane, sweet grace-nectar pleasing to the mind that walks no deceitful path, my intellect, my desire, my affection, my guru, my father, product of love, supreme bliss met in a moment devoid of night and day, light shining bright within me, pupil of my eye, precious substance granted to me starting from a plenary complete blissful life free of coming and going.
arutpa:T360:11: Ocean of grace, true guru who ruled me, complete life dancing in the great hall of wisdom, for me a dog, illusions of confusion utterly perished along with fleeing karmas, removing the great barrier of darkness, the sun indeed arose.
arutpa:T360:13: Supreme reality, light standing at the head of the Vedas, silent transcendent bliss, god performing sacred dance in the hall, stubborn illusions all perished along with fleeing karmas, removing the darkness dwelling inside, the sun indeed arose. (Kali Viruttam of Chidambaresan's grace)
arutpa:T360:155: I asked to be granted the truth that shines without ever perishing by wind, earth, sky, fire, water, sun and other luminaries, death, disease, weapons of murder, planets, or evil deeds wrought by others; he granted it swiftly to me. O people of the world, do not think of this as high or low; approach the lord, the great ocean of grace of our father.
arutpa:T346:2: Rejoice, O my companion, hear my words: I have forever attained the boon of deathlessness. I looked toward the pure eastern direction where the curving natural red flame appears, and will dance standing age after age in the glory-shining Siddhi. If you too wish, come and rule here by the king's command, wearing the ocean on your arm, and dance playing the ball, seeing the supreme vast flame and playing the ball.
arutpa:T377:24: O companion, this is the time when the graced one arrives; light a thousand, thousand million lamps, burn clear cow's ghee, do not use other ghee even if it causes a slight flaw to the sacred body. Do not think whether there is darkness or if a morning lamp needs to be lit; see, it is lit auspiciously. Do not be confused; even if the sun, moon, and red fire surpassing all numbers were to combine, it would not equal the brightness of his body.
arutpa:T377:67: Do not doubt, we are coming in the morning, this is our command—know that his command is the command of grace. The dark night that went to enter the minds of the cruel has dawned, it is the time approaching the good rising of the flame. O maiden, since I need to be alone now, stay slightly apart; once the lord arrives, I shall merge with him here, and when you and I have become one, I shall joyfully call you.
arutpa:T257:11: Grace-light dancing as one, well and good, amid the sun's own sun, in the sun's form, in natural form, in formlessness, in raised flame, in the flame within the flame, in clusters of soaring suns, in the light of one sun, in the light of soaring light, in the middle of light's light; O my close companion, my father who came that night and granted me grace-light, king, my knower, nectar, love, bliss, father, dispenser of grace, dear to my crowded life, unique, pure, my affection, treasure of pure Siva Sanmarga, O lord Nataraja of the supreme vast flame.
arutpa:T225:43: O king dancing in the bliss-hall transcending the measure of sages, who gave me something in my hand, making me—a cruel one who marked not even a whit of sharp true knowledge—walk with aching feet while sun and moon appear not, shining as a self-luminous light, walking at night and crying that there is business, and making the door open—what shall I say of your grace?
arutpa:T89:5: The sun is running, and each day others run after him. What shall we do if that cruel god of death grows angry? You wither worrying thus, do you not know the greatness of Markandeya, O heart? Do not fear; the name of the lord whom seekers seek is Namasivaya, our sustaining refuge.
tolka:540: Time, world, life, body, fate, deity, action, elements, sun, moon—saying thus, these twice-five and others of the same kind, whatever words come thus, set aside their gender and do not accord with high-class (uyartinai).
tolka:1586: Since the world is a mingling of the five—earth, fire, water, wind, and space—it is necessary that the two genders and five classes conform without straying from the natural path, combined with unchanging words.
arutpa:T158:54: Abandoning the bliss that comes, abandoning earth, abandoning sky, abandoning the striking night and day as well, abandoning separation—
arutpa:T158:87: Who is the adept capable of making the beautiful ray, which flourishes as the bright beautiful ray and as the moon, become—
arutpa:T160:23: Golden hill, completeness shining both inside and out, essence within the Vedas, sugarcane of sweet taste ever delightful to those who learn, wish-granting tree, sweet fruit of the wish-granting tree, flame of sacred grace revealing unceasing bliss within the tongue whose truthful words do not fail, flame standing in the sky, long light rising within that flame, god filled within that light.
arutpa:T160:26: Sky, wind moving in that sky, fire arising from wind, form of water originating in fire, earth abiding in that water, stationary and mobile beings dwelling in that earth, flesh, good life, inner light, inner awareness, honey oozing where those awarenesses mingle, three fruits, red sugarcane, sweet taste of molasses, honey where all tastes are gathered.
arutpa:T160:27: O sky, sky's form, sky's source, within the sky the open space, that space's shining space! O my eye, eye's pupil, eye's light, within the eye the blended sun, that sun's seed! O cool moon, cool moon's blooming cool nectar, cool nectar's essence! O melody, melody's tune, melody's essence, melody's fruit, praised and worshipped by true ascetics, O God!
arutpa:T160:70: Being the self and nothing else besides, becoming the lord of all and everything, becoming sky, wind, fire, water, and the earth with blossoming fields, and more; becoming honey, the sweet taste of honey, the fruit of sweet taste, and myself who seeks—you who stand as my lord, how can I, your dog-like slave, utter your praise?
arutpa:T127:52: Whether capable or incapable, from other humans to everyone—if not for your action, not even an atom moves! Wandering in lack, what faults have you seen in me, O good one of Otri with fertile fields, O ruby with form?
arutpa:T221:9: Within the body-forgetting soul, the light-filled one, the master of all worlds, my Nataraja, cast aside the fitting time of youth and wore the evening; though he forgot this distinct time and detached himself, I cannot forget here! Will it be agreeable to fall from asceticism into ruin? Like a subject whose king forgot him, I am poor; knowing his nature, shall I let go? Tell me, my friend.
arutpa:T3:25: Standing as earth, water, fire, wind, and sky, you grant grace as reality; with clear grace, Vishnu, Brahma, and other gods wiped their tears, O wish-granting tree, I have found you in Thanigai where the cool water and groves have wandering moons.
arutpa:T30:3: The approach of hypocrites bound with false penance vanishes; the capacity to bestow upon approaching, devoted souls multiplies. He is the reality of wind, water, fire, earth, and sky—O Siva-Shanmuga, wear the grace-giving sacred ash!
arutpa:T51:5: The red sun has risen, the gods have gathered. Come, Lord Sengalvaraya! Come, our Guru!
arutpa:T51:6: The sun has arisen, devotees have gathered. Come, Lord of the six faces! Come, Lord without a match!
arutpa:T316:30: That which is the natural state of the primeval light is the sacred assembly, the vast grace-light.
arutpa:T316:32: The assembly of that light which grants the three lights to blend and glow is the vast grace-light.
arutpa:T316:521: O True Guru who revealed the stable state of the moon, the rising state of the sun, and the resting state of fire, and all else!
arutpa:T252:8: O King whose form is grace, if you do not grant grace, who will grant grace for the darkness to vanish for this slave? O Almighty, in your grace-filled form, art itself is joined both outside and inside, shining everywhere for clarity, as the supreme grace for all leaders.
arutpa:T280:4: I rejoice in seeing him who is the food, who is the joy in food, who is the unshakable earth, who is water, who is wind, who is the sky, who is fire, who is the great ocean of grace, who appeared for the defiled to see, who appeared for me to see! I know not how to speak; he accepted all the petty words I spoke, he reached my heart, and I am joyful seeing my lord.
arutpa:T299:12: You became honey, sweet fruit, tasting sugarcane, and nectar itself; the unique reality sweetening the love of devotees! You became the sky, wind, fire, water, and the living earth; you gave grace, the rare nectar of grace.
arutpa:T257:3: Blending into all bodies, all souls, all minds, all consciousness, and all that exists, making them filled with light, removing darkness, without rising or setting at any time, shining as the ray-form of the pure Siva-shakti, as oneness, in the middle of the single consciousness-assembly called the state of singular, all-encompassing bliss—O Flame filling and shining! O Supreme seen in all oceans, all earths, all fires, all winds, all skies! O Reality spoken of by all arts as the unseen thing, O Reality that came for my eyes to see! O Intellect shining as a true companion both inside and me to touch and attain! O Treasure of pure Siva-Sanmarga, O Lord Nataraja of Vast Grace-Light!
arutpa:T368:5: In the various types of religions, citing false scriptures, you cry out with your hands, saying "Our god! Our god!" You do not know that God is one; you are greater than the elephants that fought and caused chaos! When the five-elemental body perishes, what will you do? You do not know how to make the perishable body imperishable. The time has come for my unique father to arrive for our salvation; approach here, and you will receive joy.
arutpa:T347:94: Gaining eyes that see all the billions of worlds, I came to know, like a fruit in the palm, the truth within them. To see all the billions of bodies, I speak and speak of You alone and marvel at this very birth, for you and me.
arutpa:T160:14: O God who shines as the flame of grace's rich ray in the center of the known open space, becoming rarer than the rare, beginningless and being the beginning, being grace, becoming larger than the large, being both distinct and non-distinct, shining forth as the dark and the bright, as the arts and as the reality beyond arts, transcending the instruments of perception.
arutpa:T161:103: All the sinful actions I commit in a single day are such that the sky cannot contain them, this earth cannot contain them, the worlds of the moon cannot contain them, they cannot be contained anywhere, even though He knows this—yet the gem that subdues pride ruled over me, which is a great wonder of the soul.
arutpa:T316:277: O Vast Grace-Light that created the broad space where the great elements spread in the partial expanse of the sky!
arutpa:T374:9: Long live the Lord of the great hall of gems, she said; He has come and adorned me with a garland, she said. He has granted me a body that does not perish even if aeon upon aeon passes, she said. He graced me to protect all the worlds and universes surrounded by the ocean, she said. He placed me to abide upon the seven-storied mansion, said my gentle one.
arutpa:T372:31: Who can describe, O friend, the glory of the feet of graceful mercy that dances, embodying the many natures of the seed of the five elements seen, the manifold natures of the sprouting shoot, the many, many magnificent natures at the base, the many, many natures abiding in the middle, and the endless kinds of natures adorned at the top, yet remaining unattached to those soaring things, while becoming the very conjunction of each of them?
arutpa:T372:39: Who can know and speak of the foot's greatness, O friend, which dances by moving the supreme lineage wherein, within the surrounding five elements, formless powers beyond words and mind stand without diminishing, shining each separately, bearing a fresh radiance within them so that the radiance flourishes, causing a state of power to manifest, and becoming the lords abiding within that power?
